*Sounds that are generated by turbulent / non-turbulent blood flow*
1) Flow through partial obstruction
2) Regurgitant flow backwards through incompetent valve
3) Abnormal shunting of blood between chambers
4) ↑ flow through normal valve
5) Flow into dilated valve

**Characteristics**
- Timing – systolic, diastolic, or continuous
- Intensity – by grading system (see Figure 3 below)
- Pitch – frequency (high vs. low)
	- High frequency = large pressure drops, heard from diaphragm
	- Low frequency = smaller pressure drops
- Shape – variations in intensity 
	- Constant (uniform)
	- Decrescendo (strong onset and steadily decreasing over time)
	- Crescendo-decrescendo (“diamond-shape”, ramping up to a peak and then decreasing over time
- Location – region on chest of maximum intensity by auscultation (see Figure 4 below)
- Radiation – direction of transmission of sound (usually sound follows flow direction)
	- Follows direction of pathological flow
- Response to Maneuvers – changes in quality of murmur due to specific actions
